topics.1: Moses and Aaron receive instructions from the Lord about skin infections.
topics.2: A person with a skin lesion or rash is to be examined by a priest for leprosy.
topics.3: A priest examines a skin infection; if hair turns white and the infection is deep, it is leprosy.
topics.4: A white spot not deep in the skin is to be isolated for seven days.
topics.5: After seven days, if the infection hasn't spread, it is isolated again for another seven days.
topics.6: If the infection fades and doesn't spread, the person is declared clean and must wash their clothes.
topics.7: If a white spot spreads after being declared clean, it is examined again by the priest.
topics.8: If the infection spreads, the priest declares the person unclean with leprosy.
topics.9: A person showing signs of leprosy must be brought to the priest.
topics.10: A priest examines a white spot with white hair and living flesh in it.
topics.11: A persistent leprous infection is declared unclean without isolation.
topics.12: If the infection spreads and covers the whole body, the priest examines it.
topics.13: If the infection has turned the entire skin white, the person is declared clean.
topics.14: If living flesh appears, the person is declared unclean.
topics.15: The priest sees living flesh and declares the person unclean with leprosy.
topics.16: If the living flesh turns white again, the person returns to the priest.
topics.17: The priest examines the infection again and declares the person clean if it has faded.
topics.18: A healed wound appears on the skin.
topics.19: A white or reddish-white rash appears in the healed wound and is examined by the priest.
topics.20: If the rash is lower than the skin and has white hair, it is leprosy.
topics.21: If there is no white hair and the rash is not lower than the skin, it is isolated for seven days.
topics.22: If the infection spreads, the person is declared unclean with leprosy.
topics.23: If the rash remains and does not spread, it is a scar and the person is clean.
topics.24: A burn appears on the skin and the healed skin becomes a white spot.
topics.25: If the hair in the spot turns white and the spot is lower than the skin, it is leprosy.
topics.26: If there is no white hair and the spot is not lower than the skin, it is isolated for seven days.
topics.27: After seven days, if the infection spreads, the person is declared unclean with leprosy.
topics.28: If the spot remains and does not spread, it is a scar from the burn and the person is clean.
topics.29: A person has a leprous infection on their head or beard.
topics.30: If the infection is deeper than the skin and has yellow hair, it is leprosy.
topics.31: If the infection is not deep and has no yellow hair, it is isolated for seven days.
topics.32: After seven days, if the infection hasn't spread and has no yellow hair, it is isolated again.
topics.33: The person shaves but not the bald spot, and it is isolated for another seven days.
topics.34: If the infection hasn't spread and is not deep, the person is declared clean and must wash their clothes.
topics.35: If the infection spreads after being declared clean, it is examined again.
topics.36: If the infection spreads, the person is declared unclean without checking for yellow hair.
topics.37: If the infection remains and black hair grows in it, it is declared clean.
topics.38: A person has white spots on their skin.
topics.39: If the white spots are faded, it is a harmless condition and the person is clean.
topics.40: A completely bald person is clean.
topics.41: A person bald on the front of their head is clean.
topics.42: A leprous infection appears on a bald head or the front of a bald head.
topics.43: If the infection appears white or reddish-white on a bald head, the person is leprous.
topics.44: A person with leprosy is declared unclean.
topics.45: A leprous person must wear torn clothes, let their hair grow, and announce their uncleanness.
topics.46: A leprous person must live alone outside the camp.

topics.2: The boundary goes from Bethel to Luz and the border of the Archites at Ataroth.
topics.3: The boundary descends south to the Japhletites, reaching Beth-horon the Lower and west to Gaza.
topics.4: Manasseh and Ephraim inherit the land as the descendants of Joseph.
topics.5: Ephraim's territory begins east at Ataroth and Adar, extending to Beth-horon the Upper.
topics.6: The boundary turns west to Michmash, then circles toward Taanath-shiloh and Janoah.
topics.7: The boundary goes from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, reaching Jericho and the Jordan.
topics.8: The boundary runs west from Tappuah along Canah stream. This is Ephraim's inheritance.
topics.9: Ephraim's cities are within Manasseh's territory, including all towns and surrounding areas.
topics.10: The Canaanite in Gazer was not driven out and remained in Ephraim as forced labor.

topics.1: Manasseh gets Gilead and Bashan as his tribe's inheritance because he was a warrior.
topics.2: Manasseh's other descendants are listed by their clans: Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida.
topics.3: Tzlophad, a descendant of Manasseh, has no sons only daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
topics.4: The daughters of Tzlophad ask for and receive an inheritance among their brothers as the Lord commanded.
topics.5: Manasseh's inheritance includes ten clans in addition to Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan.
topics.6: Manasseh's daughters inherit land among their brothers, and Gilead remains with the rest of Manasseh.
topics.7: Manasseh's boundary starts near Shechem and goes east to En-tappuah.
topics.8: Tappuah and En-tappuah are part of Manasseh's land but are near Ephraim's territory.
topics.9: Manasseh's boundary runs along the stream of Canah and separates it from Ephraim's land.
topics.10: Manasseh's territory is north of Ephraim with the sea as a boundary and borders with Asher and Issachar.
topics.11: Manasseh also has cities in Issachar and Asher including Beth-shean, Taanach, and Gath-rimmon.
topics.12: Manasseh could not drive out the Canaanites from their cities, so they remained.
topics.13: The Israelites grew strong and forced the Canaanites to work but did not fully remove them.
topics.14: Joseph's sons complain to Joshua that their inheritance is too small for their large population.
topics.15: Joshua tells Joseph's sons to clear the forest in the hill country of Ephraim for more land.
topics.16: Joseph's sons say the hill country is not enough because the Canaanites in the valley have iron chariots.
topics.17: Joshua tells Joseph's sons they are strong and deserve more than one inheritance.
topics.18: Joshua tells them to clear the forest and take it as their own because they are strong and the Canaanites have chariots.

topics.1: The Israelites gather at Shiloh and set up the tabernacle. The land is now under their control.
topics.2: Seven tribes of Israel have not yet received their share of the land.
topics.3: Joshua questions why the Israelites are delaying taking the land God gave them.
topics.4: Joshua instructs three men from each tribe to survey the land and report back.
topics.5: The land will be divided into seven parts. Judah will take the southern part, Joseph the northern.
topics.6: The surveyors will write the land into seven parts and bring the report. Joshua will cast lots for the tribes.
topics.7: The Levites have no inheritance because their role is the priesthood. Gad, Reuben, and half Manasseh already received their land east of the Jordan.
topics.8: Joshua sends surveyors to walk through the land and describe it. He will cast the lots in Shiloh.
topics.9: The surveyors walk through the land, describe it in a book, and return to Joshua in Shiloh.
topics.10: Joshua casts lots in Shiloh before the Lord and divides the land to the tribes as their portions.
topics.11: The tribe of Benjamin receives their inheritance by lot, between Judah and Joseph.
topics.12: Benjamin's boundary starts north of the Jordan, goes to the shoulder of Jericho, and up the mountain westward.
topics.13: The boundary turns to Luz (Bethel), then descends to Ataroth-addar on the mountain south of the valley of Achor.
topics.14: The boundary turns and encircles to the sea, reaching Kiriath-jearim, a city of Judah.
topics.15: The southern boundary starts at Kiriath-jearim and goes west to the spring of Nephtoah.
topics.16: The boundary descends to the hill facing the valley of Ben-hinnom, through the valley of Hinnom, and to the spring of En-rogel.
topics.17: The boundary turns north to the spring of En-shemesh, goes to the villages near Maaleh-adummim, and to the stone of the sons of Reuben.
topics.18: The boundary passes the hill of the Arabah northward and descends into the Arabah.
topics.19: The boundary turns to the shoulder of Beth-haccerem, and its exits reach the northern part of the Salt Sea to the edge of the Jordan.
topics.20: The Jordan River forms the eastern boundary. This is the inheritance of Benjamin with all its boundaries.
topics.21: Benjamin's cities include Jericho, Beth-haccerem, Emek-keziz, and others.
topics.22: Benjamin's cities also include Beth-arabah, Tzmarayim, and Bethel.
topics.23: Benjamin's cities include Avvim, Parah, and Efrath.
topics.24: Benjamin's cities include Kephirah-ammonah, Ofni, and Geba; twelve cities and their villages.
topics.25: Benjamin's cities include Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth.
topics.26: Benjamin's cities include Mizpeh, Cephirah, and Moza.
topics.27: Benjamin's cities include Rakkem, Yirpeel, and Taralah.
topics.28: Benjamin's cities include Tzelal-el, Jerusalem (the Jebusite), and Gibeath-kiriath-jearim; four cities and their villages.

topics.20: Issachar tribe cities Rabboth, Kishion, Abeth
topics.21: Issachar tribe cities Remeth, Ein-ganim, Ein-hadah, Beth-pazzez
topics.22: Issachar tribe boundary reaches Tabor, Shachazim, Beth-shemesh, exits to Jordan, sixteen cities with villages
topics.23: Issachar tribe inheritance includes these cities and villages
topics.24: Asher tribe gets inheritance with fifth lot
topics.25: Asher tribe boundary starts at Chelkath, Halal, Beten, Acsaph
topics.26: Asher tribe boundary reaches Carmel, sea, border of Sidonians at Lebah
topics.27: Asher tribe boundary turns east to Beth-dagon, joins Zebulun, passes Iftach-el valley, exits to Kabul
topics.28: Asher tribe boundary goes to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, Kana, up to Sidon

topics.30: Asher tribe cities Umah, Aphek, Rehob, twenty-two cities with villages
topics.31: Asher tribe inheritance includes these cities and villages
topics.32: Naphtali tribe gets inheritance with sixth lot
topics.33: Naphtali tribe boundary starts at Helef, Elon-beth-taanach, Adam-neggeb, Yabanial, up to Lakum, exits to Jordan

topics.35: Naphtali tribe fortified cities of Sidonians: Tzir, Hammat-rakkath, Kinnereth
topics.36: Naphtali tribe cities Adamah, Harumah, Chazor
topics.37: Naphtali tribe cities Kedesh, Edrei, Ein-hazor

topics.39: Naphtali tribe inheritance includes these cities and villages
topics.40: Dan tribe gets inheritance with seventh lot
topics.41: Dan tribe boundary includes Tzorah, Eshthal, Ir-shemesh
topics.42: Dan tribe cities Shaalabbin, Ayalon, Itlah
topics.43: Dan tribe cities Elon, Timnah, Ekron
topics.44: Dan tribe cities Eltekeh, Gipton, Baalath
topics.45: Dan tribe cities Jud, sons of Berak, Gat-rimon
topics.46: Dan tribe boundary includes Jordan, Rakkon, near Yafpo
topics.47: Dan tribe captures Leshem, renames it Dan after their father
topics.48: Dan tribe inheritance includes these cities and villages
topics.49: Israel completes dividing land, gives Joshua son of Nun inheritance within it

topics.1: God tells Joshua to speak to Israel about cities of refuge
topics.2: God commands Israel to assign cities of refuge as Moses instructed
topics.3: Cities of refuge protect people who kill accidentally without intent
topics.4: A killer who flees to a city must declare their case to the elders
topics.5: The city must not hand the killer to the avenger of blood if the killing was accidental
topics.6: The killer must stay in the city until the high priest dies then return home
topics.7: Three cities of refuge are set in Galilee, Ephraim, and Judah
topics.8: Three more cities of refuge are set east of Jordan in Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh
topics.9: These cities protect all Israelites and foreigners who kill accidentally

topics.3: Israel gives Levites cities and pasturelands as instructed by Yahweh.
topics.4: Kehathite families receive cities by lot from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
topics.5: Remaining Kehathite families get cities from Ephraim, Dan, and half Manasseh.
topics.6: Gershonite families receive cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and half Manasseh in Bashan.
topics.7: Merarite families get cities from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

topics.9: Cities from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin are given to Levites by name.
topics.10: Kehathite families are given the first share of cities by lot.
topics.11: Hebron in Judah is given to the Kehathites with surrounding pasturelands.
topics.12: Caleb receives the field and surrounding villages of Hebron as his inheritance.

topics.15: Holon and Debir are given to Aaron's sons with their pasturelands.

topics.17: Gibeah and Gibeon are given to Aaron's sons from Benjamin.
topics.18: Anathoth and Almon are given to Aaron's sons — four cities total.
topics.19: Aaron's sons receive thirteen cities and their pasturelands.
topics.20: Remaining Kehathite families receive cities from Ephraim.
topics.21: Shechem and Gezer are given to Kehathites as cities of refuge.
topics.22: Kibzaim and Beth-Horon are given to Kehathites — four cities total.
topics.23: Eltekeh and Gibbethon are given to Kehathites from Dan.
topics.24: Aijalon and Gat-Ramoth are given to Kehathites — four cities total.
topics.25: Taanach and Gat-Ramoth are given to Kehathites from half Manasseh — two cities total.
topics.26: Remaining Kehathite families receive ten cities and pasturelands.
topics.27: Gershonite families receive Golan and Be'erosh from half Manasseh — two cities total.
topics.28: Kishion and Daberath are given to Gershonites from Issachar.
topics.29: Yarmuth and Ein-Ganim are given to Gershonites — four cities total.
topics.30: Mishal and Abdon are given to Gershonites from Asher.
topics.31: Chelkath and Rehob are given to Gershonites — four cities total.
topics.32: Kedesh, Hammoth-Dor, and Kartan are given to Gershonites from Naphtali — three cities total.
topics.33: Gershonite families receive thirteen cities and pasturelands.
topics.34: Merarite families receive Yakan and Kartah from Zebulun.
topics.35: Dimnah and Nahalal are given to Merarites — four cities total.
topics.36: Bezer and Jahzah are given to Merarites from Reuben.
topics.37: Kedemoth and Mephaath are given to Merarites — four cities total.
topics.38: Ramoth and Mahanaim are given to Merarites from Gad as cities of refuge.
topics.39: Heshbon and Jaazer are given to Merarites — four cities total.
topics.40: Merarite families receive twelve cities and pasturelands.
topics.41: Levites receive forty-eight cities and pasturelands in Israel.
topics.42: Each Levite city has its surrounding pasturelands.
topics.43: Yahweh gives Israel the whole land He promised to their ancestors.

topics.1: Joshua speaks to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
topics.2: Joshua praises them for obeying Moses and his commands.
topics.3: He commends them for not abandoning their brothers and keeping God's commandments.
topics.4: Joshua tells them to return to their inheritance east of the Jordan River.
topics.5: He urges them to obey God's law, love Him, and serve Him wholeheartedly.
topics.6: Joshua blesses and sends them back to their homes.
topics.7: Moses had given half of Manasseh land in Bashan, and Joshua gave the other half.
topics.8: Joshua tells them to return with riches and share their spoils with their brothers.
topics.9: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh leave from Shechem to return home.
topics.10: They build a large altar at the Jordan River as a visible sign.
topics.11: The Israelites hear about the altar built by Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
topics.12: The Israelites gather at Shiloh to prepare to go to war against them.
topics.13: The Israelites send Phinehas the priest and ten tribal leaders to Gilead.
topics.14: The leaders are from each tribe and represent the thousands of Israel.
topics.15: They confront the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh about the altar.
topics.16: The Israelites accuse them of rebelling against God by building a separate altar.
topics.17: They remind them of the sin of Peor and the resulting plague.
topics.18: They warn that God's anger will flare up against all Israel if they rebel.
topics.19: They suggest the tribes move to the land of the tabernacle if their land is unclean.
topics.20: They reference Achan's sin and how he alone bore the consequences.
topics.21: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh respond to the leaders.
topics.22: They swear they have not rebelled against God and ask Him to judge.
topics.23: They clarify the altar is not for sacrifices but to show unity with Israel.
topics.24: They explain the altar is to prevent future generations from forgetting God.
topics.25: They fear the Jordan River will become a barrier between them and Israel.
topics.26: They clarify the altar is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices.
topics.27: They say the altar is a witness to their shared worship of God.
topics.28: They explain the altar's purpose to future generations.
topics.29: They reaffirm their loyalty to God and the central altar in the tabernacle.
topics.30: Phinehas and the leaders hear their explanation and are satisfied.
topics.31: Phinehas declares the Israelites know God is with them and they did not rebel.
topics.32: Phinehas and the leaders return to Israel and report back.
topics.33: The Israelites are pleased and do not go to war against the tribes.
topics.34: The tribes name the altar as a witness that God is the one true God.

topics.7: Israel must not associate with remaining nations or their gods
topics.8: Joshua tells Israel to remain faithful to God as they have been
topics.9: God will defeat powerful nations and no one has resisted Israel
topics.10: One Israelite can chase a thousand because God fights for them
topics.11: Joshua urges Israel to carefully love God
topics.12: If Israel intermarries with remaining nations, disaster will follow
topics.13: If Israel turns to other gods, the nations will trap and destroy them
topics.14: Joshua says all of God's promises have come true for Israel

topics.12: God sent hornets to drive out the Amorites without Israel's weapons
topics.13: God gave Israel land, cities, and vineyards they did not build or plant
topics.14: Joshua urges Israel to serve God alone and remove foreign gods

topics.1: Israel asks God who will lead them to fight the Canaanites after Joshua's death.

topics.3: Judah invites Simeon to fight together in each other's territories.

topics.1: Israelites do evil, Ehud dies

topics.29: Solomon has large labor forces for carrying and cutting stone
topics.30: Supervisors oversee the workers and manage the construction project
topics.31: The king orders the quarrying of large, costly stones for the temple foundation
topics.32: Builders from Solomon, Hiram, and Giblites prepare materials for the temple

topics.1: Solomon begins building the temple 480 years after Israel left Egypt
topics.2: Solomon builds the temple 60 cubits long, 20 wide, 30 high
topics.3: Solomon builds a porch 20 cubits long, 10 wide
topics.4: Solomon installs latticed windows in the temple
topics.5: Solomon builds walls and decorative beams around the temple
topics.6: Temple has three levels with increasing width to support the structure
topics.7: Temple built with perfectly cut stones, no metal tools used
topics.8: Middle story entrance on the right, spiral stairs to upper levels
topics.9: Solomon completes the temple construction
topics.10: Solomon builds side rooms around the temple, fastened with cedar
topics.11: God speaks to Solomon about the temple
topics.12: God promises to dwell with Israel if they follow His laws
topics.13: God promises not to abandon Israel
topics.14: Solomon completes the temple
topics.15: Solomon lines the temple walls with cedar and cypress
topics.16: Solomon builds cedar-lined sections of the temple and the Holy of Holies
topics.17: The temple is 40 cubits long in front
topics.18: Solomon decorates the temple with cedar carvings, no stone visible
topics.19: Solomon prepares the inner chamber for the ark of the covenant
topics.20: Solomon builds a 20-cubit chamber in front of the Holy of Holies, overlaid with gold
topics.21: Solomon overlays the temple with gold and makes gold chains for the inner chamber
topics.22: Solomon covers the entire temple and altar with gold
topics.23: Solomon makes two ten-cubit cherubim of carved wood
topics.24: Each cherub has a five-cubit wingspan, total ten cubits together
topics.25: Both cherubim are ten cubits tall, measured the same
topics.26: Each cherub is ten cubits tall
topics.27: Cherubim placed in the innermost part of the temple, wings touching walls and each other
topics.28: Solomon overlays the cherubim with gold
topics.29: Solomon carves cherubim, palm trees, and openwork designs on all temple walls
topics.30: Solomon overlays the temple floor with gold, inside and out
topics.31: Solomon makes five-panel olive wood doors for the inner chamber
topics.32: Solomon makes two olive wood doors with gold cherubim and palm carvings
topics.33: Solomon makes four-panel olive wood doors for the temple porch
topics.34: Solomon makes two cypress wood doors, each with two panels
topics.35: Solomon carves cherubim, palm trees, and openwork on the doors, then overlays with gold
topics.36: Solomon builds the inner courtyard with three rows of stone and cedar beams
topics.37: The temple foundation is laid in the fourth year, month of Ziv
topics.38: The temple is completed in the eleventh year, month of Bul, after seven years of construction

topics.1: Solomon builds his palace in thirteen years, completing all parts of it.
topics.2: The palace is built from cedarwood, with specific dimensions and decorative pillars.
topics.3: Cedarwood overlays the beams above the side rooms, with precise measurements.
topics.4: Three projecting structures are built, each with a matching room opposite it.
topics.5: All doorways and doorposts are square, with projecting and retracted designs.
topics.6: The porch of the pillars is built with specific dimensions and decorative elements.
topics.7: The judgment hall is built with cedarwood from floor to ceiling.
topics.8: Solomon builds a house for Pharaoh's daughter similar to the palace's design.
topics.9: Expensive, precisely cut stones are used throughout the palace and courtyards.
topics.10: Large, costly stones are laid in the palace, including ten- and eight-cubit stones.
topics.11: Top layers use precise measurements and cedarwood for finishing.
topics.12: The great courtyard has hewn stone and cedarwood beams, matching inner structures.
topics.13: Solomon sends for Hiram from Tyre to assist in construction.
topics.14: Hiram, a bronze craftsman from Naphtali, is skilled and works for Solomon.
topics.15: Hiram casts two bronze pillars, each eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits around.
topics.16: Two bronze capitals are made, each five cubits tall, to top the pillars.
topics.17: Chains and threads are crafted for the capitals, seven on each.
topics.18: Hiram finishes the pillars with chainwork, covering the capitals.
topics.19: The capitals are lily-shaped, with a four-cubit design in the porch.
topics.20: Additional bronze details are added to the capitals, including pomegranates and two rows.
topics.21: The pillars are set in the temple porch, named Yachin and Boaz.
topics.22: Lily-shaped designs top the pillars, completing their construction.
topics.23: A large bronze basin, ten cubits in diameter and five cubits high, is made.
topics.24: Pomegranates are cast around the basin, in two rows.
topics.25: The basin rests on twelve bronze oxen, each facing a cardinal direction.
topics.26: The basin has a thick rim and lily-shaped pomegranates around it.
topics.27: Ten bronze stands are made, each with specific dimensions.
topics.28: The stands have latches and crossbars for structural design.
topics.29: Lions, oxen, and cherubim are engraved on the latches and crossbars.
topics.30: Each stand has four bronze wheels and axles cast as a single piece.
topics.31: The stand's basin is round with square latches and handles.
topics.32: Wheels are attached under the latches, with specific dimensions.
topics.33: The wheels are cast like chariot wheels, with handles and hubs.
topics.34: Each stand has four brackets attached to its corners.
topics.35: The stand's top has a round rim with handles and latches.
topics.36: Cherubim, lions, and palm trees are carved into the handles and latches.
topics.37: All ten stands are made identically, with the same measurements and design.
topics.38: Ten bronze basins are made, each holding forty seahs of water.
topics.39: The stands are placed on both sides of the temple, and the basin is on the right side.
topics.40: Hiram completes all the bronze work for the temple, including basins and tools.
topics.41: Two pillars, two capitals, and two chainworks are made for the temple.
topics.42: Four hundred pomegranates are cast for the chainworks, covering the capitals.
topics.43: Ten stands and ten basins are placed on the stands.
topics.44: One large basin and twelve oxen are placed under the basin.
topics.45: All bronze tools and vessels made by Hiram are hammered bronze.
topics.46: The bronze items are cast in the Jordan River area between Sukkoth and Tzarten.
topics.47: Solomon places all the bronze items in the temple, in great abundance.
topics.48: Solomon makes all the temple vessels, including the golden altar and table.
topics.49: Ten golden lampstands are placed in the inner sanctuary, with golden details.
topics.50: Golden siphons, ladles, and door handles are made for the holy areas.
topics.51: Solomon completes the temple work and places David's holy items in the treasuries.

topics.1: Solomon gathers Israel's leaders to bring the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem from Zion.
topics.2: All Israel gathers in Jerusalem in the seventh month for a festival as Solomon prepares to bring the Ark.
topics.3: Elders of Israel arrive, and priests carry the Ark of the Covenant.
topics.4: Priests and Levites bring the Ark, Tent of Meeting, and sacred items to the temple.
topics.5: Solomon and the assembly offer countless sacrifices of sheep and oxen before the Ark.
topics.6: Priests place the Ark in the Most Holy Place under the cherubim's wings in the temple.
topics.7: Cherubim spread wings over the Ark and cover it from above in the Most Holy Place.
topics.8: The Ark's poles extend into the Holy Place but not outside, remaining there to this day.
topics.9: Only the two stone tablets given to Moses at Horeb are in the Ark, representing the covenant with Israel.
topics.10: Cloud fills the temple as the priests exit the Most Holy Place.
topics.11: Priests cannot minister due to the cloud, as the glory of the LORD fills the temple.
topics.12: Solomon declares the LORD dwells in thick darkness, not in human-built structures.
topics.13: Solomon says he built a glorious house for the LORD to dwell in forever.
topics.14: Solomon turns to bless the assembly of Israel, who stand before him.
topics.15: Solomon praises the LORD for fulfilling the promise to David and Israel.
topics.16: God did not choose a city for a temple but chose David to lead Israel.
topics.17: David wanted to build a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.
topics.18: God praised David's desire to build a temple, though he did not build it.
topics.19: God promised David's son would build the temple for His name.
topics.20: God kept His promise to David, and Solomon built the temple for the LORD.
topics.21: Solomon placed the Ark in the temple, where the covenant with Israel was kept.
topics.22: Solomon stands before the altar with hands spread to heaven and begins to pray.
topics.23: Solomon declares the LORD is the only true God, faithful to His covenant and love.
topics.24: God kept His word to David, fulfilling His promises with power.
topics.25: Solomon asks the LORD to keep the promise to David about the throne of Israel.
topics.26: Solomon asks the LORD to confirm His promise to David, his father.
topics.27: Solomon questions whether God can truly dwell in a temple built by humans.
topics.28: Solomon asks the LORD to listen to his prayer and the people's plea before Him.
topics.29: Solomon asks the LORD to always watch over the temple and hear prayers offered there.
topics.30: Solomon asks the LORD to hear prayers from Israel and forgive their sins from heaven.
topics.31: Solomon asks the LORD to judge oaths and ensure justice for those who swear falsely.
topics.32: Solomon asks the LORD to judge the guilty and vindicate the righteous.
topics.33: Solomon asks the LORD to forgive Israel's sins and restore them to the land when they repent.
topics.34: Solomon asks the LORD to forgive Israel's sins and return them to the land given to their ancestors.
topics.35: Solomon asks the LORD to send rain when Israel repents after a drought.
topics.36: Solomon asks the LORD to forgive sins, guide Israel, and send rain on the land.
topics.37: Solomon asks the LORD to hear prayers for relief from famine, plague, or war.
topics.38: Solomon asks the LORD to hear every person's prayer for their troubles toward the temple.
topics.39: Solomon asks the LORD to know every person's heart and act justly.
topics.40: Solomon asks the LORD to let Israel fear Him all their lives in the land given to their ancestors.
topics.41: Solomon asks the LORD to hear prayers from foreigners who come to the temple because of His name.
topics.42: Solomon asks the LORD to hear foreigners who come because of His great name and mighty power.
topics.43: Solomon asks the LORD to let all nations know His name and fear Him through the temple.
topics.44: Solomon asks the LORD to hear Israel's prayers when they go to war.
topics.45: Solomon asks the LORD to act justly for Israel when they pray in battle.
topics.46: Solomon acknowledges Israel will sin, be punished, and taken to a distant land.
topics.47: Solomon asks the LORD to hear Israel's repentance and prayers when they return to Him in captivity.
topics.48: Solomon asks the LORD to hear Israel's prayers from the land of their captors toward the temple.
topics.49: Solomon asks the LORD to hear Israel's prayers and act justly for them in captivity.
topics.50: Solomon asks the LORD to forgive Israel's sins and show mercy to them in captivity.
topics.51: Solomon reminds the LORD that Israel is His inheritance, brought out of Egypt.
topics.52: Solomon asks the LORD to always hear the prayers of His servant and His people.
topics.53: Solomon reminds the LORD that Israel is His chosen people, as promised to Moses.
topics.54: Solomon finishes his prayer, rises from the altar, and spreads his hands to heaven.
topics.55: Solomon blesses the assembly of Israel with a loud voice.
topics.56: Solomon declares the LORD has fulfilled all His promises to Israel through Moses.
topics.57: Solomon asks the LORD to be with Israel as He was with their ancestors.
topics.58: Solomon asks the LORD to turn Israel's hearts to Him and keep His commandments.
topics.59: Solomon asks the LORD to remember his prayers and act justly for Israel every day.
topics.60: Solomon asks the LORD to let all nations know He is the only true God.
topics.61: Solomon asks the LORD to keep Israel's hearts whole and faithful to His commandments.
topics.62: Solomon and all Israel offer sacrifices before the LORD at the temple.
topics.63: Solomon offers peace offerings, 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep, to dedicate the temple.
topics.64: Solomon dedicates the temple courtyard because the bronze altar could not hold all the sacrifices.
topics.65: Solomon holds a great festival with all Israel, from Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, for 14 days.
topics.66: After the festival, the people leave, blessed and joyful, praising the LORD's goodness to David and Israel.

topics.1: Solomon finishes building the temple and his palace
topics.2: God appears to Solomon a second time at Gibeon
topics.3: God promises to honor Solomon's prayer and keep His presence in the temple
topics.4: God tells Solomon to walk in obedience like David did
topics.5: God promises Solomon's dynasty will last forever like David's
topics.6: God warns Solomon about turning to other gods
topics.7: God threatens to destroy Israel and the temple if they disobey
topics.8: The temple will become a ruin and people will wonder why
topics.9: People will say Israel was punished for abandoning God
topics.10: Solomon spent twenty years building the temple and palace
topics.11: Hiram of Tyre supplies Solomon with cedar, fir, and gold
topics.12: Hiram visits the cities given to him by Solomon
topics.13: Hiram is unhappy with the cities and calls them Cabul
topics.14: Hiram sends Solomon 120 talents of gold
topics.15: Solomon imposes a tax to build the temple, palace, and cities
topics.16: Pharaoh of Egypt captures and burns Gezer, gives it to Solomon's wife
topics.17: Solomon rebuilds Gezer and Beth Horon the Lower
topics.18: Solomon builds Baalah (Tadmor) and storage and military cities
topics.19: Solomon builds storehouses, chariot cities, and horse cities across his kingdom
topics.20: Leftover Canaanite tribes remain in the land
topics.21: Solomon forces the Canaanite descendants to pay tribute
topics.22: Israelites are not forced into labor but serve in government and military
topics.23: Solomon appoints 550 overseers to manage laborers
topics.24: Pharaoh's daughter moves into her palace in Jerusalem
topics.25: Solomon offers sacrifices three times a year at the temple
topics.26: Solomon builds a fleet at Ezion-Geber on the Red Sea
topics.27: Hiram sends sailors to help Solomon's fleet
topics.28: Solomon's fleet returns with 420 talents of gold from Ophir

topics.1: The Queen of Sheba hears about Solomon's wisdom and reputation for God and decides to test him.
topics.2: The Queen of Sheba arrives in Jerusalem with a large caravan of camels carrying spices, gold, and precious stones.
topics.3: Solomon answers all the Queen of Sheba's questions, leaving nothing unanswered.
topics.4: The Queen of Sheba sees Solomon's wisdom and the grandeur of the temple he built.
topics.5: The Queen of Sheba is overwhelmed by the royal meals, servants, attendants, and offerings at Solomon's court and the temple.
topics.6: The Queen of Sheba confirms that the stories about Solomon's wisdom and words were true.
topics.7: The Queen of Sheba admits the reality of Solomon's wisdom was even greater than what she had heard.
topics.8: The Queen of Sheba praises Solomon's servants and attendants for hearing his wisdom.
topics.9: The Queen of Sheba praises God for choosing Solomon to rule Israel with justice and love.
topics.10: The Queen of Sheba gives Solomon a large gift of gold, spices, and precious stones.
topics.11: A ship from Hiram brings cedar and juniper wood and precious stones from Ophir to Solomon.
topics.12: Solomon uses the cedar wood to make supports for the temple and palace, and instruments for singers.
topics.13: Solomon gives the Queen of Sheba everything she asked for, and she returns to her homeland.
topics.14: In one year, Solomon receives 666 talents of gold.
topics.15: The gold comes from traders, regional kings, and officials in addition to regular tribute.
topics.16: Solomon makes 200 shields of hammered gold, each weighing 600 shekels.
topics.17: Solomon makes 300 gold shields, each weighing 3 minas, and stores them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
topics.18: Solomon builds a large ivory throne and covers it with pure gold.
topics.19: Solomon's throne has six steps, lions carved on the back, and two lions on the arms.
topics.20: Twelve lions stand on the six steps of the throne; no other kingdom has such a throne.
topics.21: All of Solomon's drinking vessels and items in the House of the Forest of Lebanon are made of gold. Silver is worthless.
topics.22: A ship from Tarshish arrives every three years with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
topics.23: Solomon becomes the richest and wisest king in the world.
topics.24: People from all over the world come to hear Solomon's wisdom, given by God.
topics.25: Each year, people bring silver, gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules as tribute to Solomon.
topics.26: Solomon gathers 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, keeping them in chariot cities and Jerusalem.
topics.27: Solomon treats silver and cedar like common materials due to their abundance.
topics.28: Solomon's horses come from Egypt and Kue, bought by royal merchants.
topics.29: A chariot costs 600 silver shekels and a horse 150, as sold to Hittite and Aramean kings.

topics.1: Solomon marries many foreign women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and Hittite lands.
topics.2: God warned Israel not to intermarry with these nations, as they lead to idolatry.
topics.3: Solomon has 700 wives and 300 concubines, and they influence him negatively.
topics.4: In his old age, Solomon’s foreign wives lead him to worship other gods, unlike his father David.
topics.5: Solomon follows Ashtoreth, the Sidonian goddess, and Milcom, the Ammonite god.
topics.6: Solomon does evil in God’s eyes and does not follow the LORD like David did.
topics.7: Solomon builds altars for Chemosh, the Moabite god, and Milcom, the Ammonite god.
topics.8: Solomon builds altars and offers sacrifices to the gods of his foreign wives.
topics.9: God becomes angry with Solomon for turning away from Him, despite His appearances.
topics.10: God had warned Solomon not to follow other gods, but he ignored the command.
topics.11: God says He will take the kingdom from Solomon for breaking His covenant and laws.
topics.12: God will not act during Solomon’s lifetime, but will take the kingdom from his son.
topics.13: God promises to leave one tribe for David’s sake and for Jerusalem.
topics.14: God raises up Hadad, an Edomite prince, as a threat to Solomon’s reign.
topics.15: Hadad fled after Joab killed all the Edomite men during David’s time.
topics.16: Joab and Israel stayed in Edom for six months to kill every male.
topics.17: Hadad was a young man when he fled to Egypt with his father’s servants.
topics.18: Hadad went to Pharaoh in Egypt and was given food, a house, and support.
topics.19: Pharaoh gave Hadad his sister in marriage, the queen’s sister.
topics.20: Tahpenes, the queen, raised Hadad’s son Genubath in Pharaoh’s palace.
topics.21: Hadad heard that David and Joab had died and asked Pharaoh to return to Edom.
topics.22: Pharaoh questioned why Hadad wanted to leave, but let him go.
topics.23: God also raised up Rezon, a former servant of Hadadezer, as a threat to Israel.
topics.24: Rezon became a leader in Damascus and ruled there after fighting under David.
topics.25: Rezon and Hadad caused trouble for Israel during Solomon’s reign.
topics.26: Jeroboam, an Ephrathite from Zeredah, was a servant to Solomon and later rebelled.
topics.27: Jeroboam rebelled after Solomon built the Millo and fortified David’s city.
topics.28: Jeroboam was strong and hardworking, so Solomon made him overseer of the house of Joseph.
topics.29: The prophet Ahijah met Jeroboam on the road and gave him a divine message.
topics.30: Ahijah tore his new cloak into twelve pieces to symbolize God’s message.
topics.31: God told Jeroboam He would give him ten tribes of Israel, tearing the kingdom from Solomon.
topics.32: One tribe would remain with Solomon’s son for David’s and Jerusalem’s sake.
topics.33: God is angry because Israel has abandoned Him and worshipped foreign gods.
topics.34: God will not take the whole kingdom from Solomon during his lifetime for David’s sake.
topics.35: God will give ten tribes to Jeroboam and leave one for Solomon’s son.
topics.36: The remaining tribe will be a light for David in Jerusalem, where God put His name.
topics.37: God promises Jeroboam he will be king over Israel if he follows God’s ways.
topics.38: If Jeroboam obeys God and keeps His laws, God will build him a lasting dynasty.
topics.39: God will punish David’s descendants for this, but not forever.
topics.40: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, who fled to Egypt and stayed until Solomon’s death.
topics.41: The full account of Solomon’s life and wisdom is written in the Book of the Words of Solomon.
topics.42: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over Israel for forty years.
topics.43: Solomon died and was buried in David’s city, and his son Rehoboam became king.

topics.1: Rehoboam goes to Shechem where all Israel has gathered to make him king.
topics.2: Jeroboam, who fled from Solomon to Egypt, hears about the gathering in Shechem.
topics.3: Jeroboam is summoned to Shechem and joins the assembly with all Israel.
topics.4: The people ask Rehoboam to lighten the heavy burdens imposed by his father.
topics.5: Rehoboam tells the people to return in three days, and they leave.
topics.6: Rehoboam consults with the elders who served Solomon for advice on the people’s request.
topics.7: The elders advise Rehoboam to be kind and speak gently to win the people’s loyalty.
topics.8: Rehoboam ignores the elders and asks the young men for advice instead.
topics.9: Rehoboam asks the young men what to say to the people who want lighter burdens.
topics.10: The young men advise Rehoboam to threaten the people and promise harsher treatment.
topics.11: Rehoboam replies to the people with harsh words, promising to add to their burdens.
topics.12: The people return to Rehoboam on the third day as he had told them.
topics.13: Rehoboam gives a harsh reply to the people, ignoring the elders’ advice.
topics.14: Rehoboam repeats the young men’s advice, promising to increase the people’s suffering.
topics.15: The king’s harsh response fulfills the LORD’s word through Ahijah to Jeroboam.
topics.16: Israel rebels against Rehoboam, rejecting David’s house and returning to their homes.
topics.17: The Israelites in Judah remain under Rehoboam’s rule.
topics.18: Rehoboam sends Adoram to collect taxes, but the people stone him to death and he flees.
topics.19: Israel has been in rebellion against David’s house ever since.
topics.20: Israel hears Rehoboam has returned and makes Jeroboam king over all Israel except Judah.
topics.21: Rehoboam gathers 180,000 warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel.
topics.22: The word of the LORD comes to Shemaiah the man of God.
topics.23: The LORD tells Shemaiah to command Rehoboam not to go to war with Israel.
topics.24: The LORD orders Rehoboam to return home, and the people obey.
topics.25: Jeroboam builds up Shechem and Penuel in the hill country of Ephraim.
topics.26: Jeroboam fears the kingdom will return to David’s house.
topics.27: Jeroboam worries the people will return to Jerusalem and Rehoboam, endangering him.
topics.28: Jeroboam makes two golden calves and tells the people they are their gods.
topics.29: One golden calf is placed in Bethel and the other in Dan.
topics.30: The golden calves become a sin, and the people worship them as far as Dan.
topics.31: Jeroboam builds high places and appoints non-Levite priests.
topics.32: Jeroboam creates a festival in Bethel like the one in Judah and offers sacrifices.
topics.33: Jeroboam holds a festival on the fifteenth of the eighth month and offers sacrifices.

topics.1: A prophet from Judah arrives at Bethel where Jeroboam is offering incense
topics.2: The prophet declares a future king will destroy the altar and priests of Bethel
topics.3: The prophet predicts the altar will split and its ashes spill out
topics.4: Jeroboam tries to arrest the prophet but his hand becomes paralyzed
topics.5: The altar splits and ashes spill out as the prophet foretold
topics.6: The prophet prays for Jeroboam and his hand is healed
topics.7: Jeroboam offers the prophet food and a gift to stay with him
topics.8: The prophet refuses to accept Jeroboam's offer or return with him
topics.9: The prophet explains he was commanded not to eat or return the way he came
topics.10: The prophet takes a different route and does not return to Bethel
topics.11: An old prophet in Bethel learns about the man of God's actions and words
topics.12: The old prophet asks which way the prophet went and his sons show him
topics.13: The old prophet saddles his donkey and sets out to find the prophet
topics.14: The old prophet finds the prophet under a tree and asks if he is the man from Judah
topics.15: The old prophet invites the prophet to his home to eat
topics.16: The prophet refuses to eat or drink with the old prophet in that place
topics.17: The prophet explains he was commanded not to eat or return the way he came
topics.18: The old prophet reveals he is also a prophet and was told to bring the prophet home
topics.19: The old prophet brings the prophet home and they eat and drink together
topics.20: The word of the Lord comes to the old prophet while they are eating
topics.21: The Lord condemns the prophet for disobeying and eating in the forbidden place
topics.22: The Lord declares the prophet will not be buried with his ancestors
topics.23: The old prophet saddles the donkey for the prophet to continue his journey
topics.24: A lion attacks and kills the prophet on the road
topics.25: Passersby see the prophet's body and the lion and report it to the old prophet
topics.26: The old prophet confirms the Lord's judgment was fulfilled by the lion's attack
topics.27: The old prophet saddles his donkey to go and retrieve the prophet's body
topics.28: The old prophet finds the prophet's body and the lion and donkey still there
topics.29: The old prophet places the prophet's body on the donkey and returns to mourn
topics.30: The prophet is buried and mourned by the old prophet and his sons
topics.31: The old prophet instructs his sons to bury him with the prophet in the same tomb
topics.32: The old prophet says the Lord's prophecy about the altar will be fulfilled
topics.33: Jeroboam continues his evil ways and appoints unqualified priests
topics.34: The Lord's judgment on Jeroboam's house leads to its destruction

topics.1: Abijah, son of Jeroboam, becomes ill
topics.2: Jeroboam tells his wife to disguise and visit a prophet in Shiloh
topics.3: Jeroboam's wife instructed to bring bread, fig cakes, and honey to the prophet
topics.4: Jeroboam's wife goes to Shiloh and enters the prophet Ahijah's house
topics.5: God tells Ahijah that Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask about her son
topics.6: Ahijah recognizes Jeroboam's disguised wife and warns her of a difficult message
topics.7: Ahijah delivers a message from God to Jeroboam about his rise to power
topics.8: God compares Jeroboam to David and criticizes his failure to follow commandments
topics.9: God condemns Jeroboam for making idols and turning away from Him
topics.10: God declares judgment on Jeroboam's house, threatening to destroy all males
topics.11: God says the dead will be eaten by dogs and birds as punishment
topics.12: Ahijah tells Jeroboam's wife the boy will die when she returns to the city
topics.13: Abijah will be mourned and buried, the only one in Jeroboam's house to find favor
topics.14: God promises to raise a new king to destroy Jeroboam's house
topics.15: God warns Israel will be scattered for making idols and provoking Him
topics.16: Israel's punishment is due to Jeroboam's sins and leading others astray
topics.17: Jeroboam's wife returns to find her son dead at the threshold of their house
topics.18: Abijah is buried and mourned by all Israel as prophesied
topics.19: Details of Jeroboam's reign and wars are recorded in the Book of Chronicles
topics.20: Jeroboam dies after a 22-year reign, succeeded by his son Nadab
topics.21: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, begins his 17-year reign in Jerusalem
topics.22: Rehoboam leads Judah into sin, angering God with their actions
topics.23: Judah builds high places, pillars, and Asherahs in the hills and under trees
topics.24: Prostitution and detestable practices spread in Judah like other nations
topics.25: Shishak, king of Egypt, attacks Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year
topics.26: Shishak takes treasures from the temple and the king's house, including gold shields

topics.4: Jeremiah promises to pray and tell them everything God says
topics.5: The people swear to obey whatever God tells Jeremiah to say

topics.7: After ten days, God speaks to Jeremiah
topics.8: Jeremiah calls for Johanan, the commanders, and the whole people
topics.9: God says he was sent to intercede for them with prayer
topics.10: God says if they stay and build, he will not destroy them
topics.11: God says not to fear the king of Babylon because he will rescue them
topics.12: God promises to show compassion and bring them back to their land
topics.13: God warns them if they refuse to stay and instead go to Egypt

topics.1: Jeremiah finishes speaking to the people all the words of the Lord his God that were sent to them.
topics.2: Azariah, Johanan, and others accuse Jeremiah of lying about not being sent to forbid them from going to Egypt.
topics.3: They claim Baruch has deceived Jeremiah to hand them over to the Chaldeans for death and exile.
topics.4: Johanan and the army commanders and people ignore the Lord's command to stay in Judah.
topics.5: Johanan and the commanders take the remaining people of Judah to live in the land of Judah.

topics.8: The word of the Lord comes to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes.
topics.9: The Lord tells Jeremiah to hide large stones in the mortar at Pharaoh's gate in Tahpanhes in front of the Judeans.
topics.10: Jeremiah is to tell them the Lord will send Nebuchadnezzar to set his throne above the stones and strike Egypt.
topics.11: Nebuchadnezzar will destroy Egypt with death, captivity, and the sword.
topics.12: The Lord will burn the gods' houses in Egypt and devastate the land as a shepherd tears his cloak.
topics.13: He will destroy the pillars of the sun temple and burn the houses of Egyptian gods with fire.

topics.1: Baruch writes Jeremiah's words on a scroll during Jehoiakim's reign
topics.2: God speaks a message directly to Baruch
topics.3: Baruch complains of grief and lack of rest
topics.4: God says he will destroy what he built and planted
topics.5: God warns Baruch not to seek greatness and that disaster is coming

topics.1: God announces a destructive wind is coming against Babylon and its people.
topics.2: Foreign invaders will attack and plunder Babylon as it faces disaster.
topics.3: Warriors are called to prepare for battle and show no mercy to Babylon's youth.
topics.4: Many will be killed in Babylon and its surrounding areas during the attack.
topics.5: Israel and Judah are not abandoned by God, but their land is filled with sin.
topics.6: People are urged to flee Babylon quickly as God's judgment is coming.
topics.7: Babylon is like a golden cup that has made the nations drunk and unstable.
topics.8: Babylon has suddenly fallen, and people are told to mourn and try to heal it.
topics.9: Efforts to heal Babylon have failed, and its judgment is as high as the heavens.
topics.10: God's judgment is revealed, and people are called to proclaim it in Zion.
topics.11: God stirs up the Medes to attack Babylon as part of His plan for revenge.
topics.12: A signal is raised on Babylon's walls as God prepares to carry out His plan.
topics.13: Babylon is described as a city with many riches and water, but its end is near.
topics.14: God swears to destroy Babylon, filling it with people like grasshoppers.

topics.16: God controls the rain, clouds, and wind, showing His power over nature.
topics.17: People are foolish, and their idols are lifeless and false.
topics.18: Idols are empty and will disappear when God's judgment comes.
topics.19: Jacob's God is the true creator, unlike the false gods of Babylon.
topics.20: Babylon will be used by God to destroy nations and their rulers.
topics.21: God will scatter Babylon's horses, riders, and chariots.
topics.22: Men, women, children, and warriors will all be scattered by Babylon's power.
topics.23: Shepherds, farmers, and leaders will be destroyed with their flocks and harvests.
topics.24: God will repay Babylon for the harm it caused to Zion and Jerusalem.
topics.25: God is coming as a mountain of destruction to destroy Babylon.
topics.26: Babylon will be left as a ruin, with no stones used for building.
topics.27: A call is made to nations and kings to prepare for war against Babylon.

topics.35: Zion and Jerusalem lament the suffering and bloodshed caused by Babylon.
topics.36: God promises to judge Babylon, dry up its rivers, and stop its springs.
topics.37: Babylon will become a ruin and a home for wild animals.
topics.38: The people of Babylon will cry like jackals and howl like lion cubs.
topics.39: God will make Babylon's people drunk so they can sleep forever.
topics.40: Babylon's people will be destroyed like rams and lambs to the slaughter.
topics.41: Babylon, once a glory of the world, is now captured and ruined.
topics.42: The sea will cover Babylon with its waves, destroying it.
topics.43: Babylon's cities become deserts, with no people or travelers.
topics.44: God will destroy the idols of Babylon, including Bel and Marduk.

topics.58: Babylon's walls and gates will be destroyed, and its people will be exhausted.

topics.61: Seraiah is told to read the book in Babylon and speak the words.
topics.62: He is to declare that God will destroy Babylon forever.

topics.1: Jerusalem sits alone, once great among nations, now in slavery and shame.
topics.2: She weeps at night, with no comfort, lovers and neighbors turned to enemies.
topics.3: Judah was taken into exile, with no rest, pursued in her distress.
topics.4: Zion's roads mourn, gates are empty, priests and virgins taken, bitterness overwhelms her.
topics.5: Her enemies rule her, the Lord caused her suffering for her sins, children captured.
topics.6: Jerusalem's glory is gone, leaders like deer without food, fleeing the enemy.
topics.7: Remember Jerusalem's past glory, now mocked, enemies laugh at her festivals.
topics.8: Jerusalem sinned, is rejected, honored ones despise her, she groans and turns away.
topics.9: She is defiled, forgotten her former days, in dire need, no comfort, enemy is strong.
topics.10: Enemy took her treasures, nations entered her holy place, which the Lord forbade.
topics.11: People groan for food, gave treasures for survival, Lord see my ruin.
topics.12: Passersby look at her sorrow, is there any pain like this, caused by the Lord's anger?

topics.16: I weep, eyes overflow, no comfort, children lost, enemy prevailed.

topics.19: I called to my friends, they betrayed me, priests and elders died seeking food.
topics.20: Lord, I am in deep pain, heart broken, soul shaken, sword pierced my home.
topics.21: I cry with no comfort, enemies heard and rejoiced, you brought this day.
topics.22: Let their evil come before you, treat them as me, my sorrows are many, heart grieved.

topics.7: Lot rescued from the corrupt city he lived in

topics.1: A second letter to believers, reminding them of important truths and encouraging sincere minds.
topics.2: Believers are urged to remember the words of holy prophets and the commands of the Lord and Savior.
topics.3: Mockers will arise in the last days, following their own desires and rejecting truth.
topics.4: Mockers question where is the promise of the Lord's return, claiming everything remains unchanged.
topics.5: They ignore that the heavens and earth were created by God's word, from and through water.
topics.6: The ancient world was destroyed by a flood, a historical example of God's judgment.
topics.7: The current heavens and earth are stored for fire, reserved for judgment and destruction of the wicked.
topics.8: A reminder that one day with the Lord is like a thousand years, and vice versa.
topics.9: The Lord is not slow in keeping his promise but is patient, wanting all to repent and not perish.
topics.10: The day of the Lord will come suddenly, destroying the heavens and earth with fire.
topics.11: Since everything will be destroyed, believers must live in holy conduct and godliness.
topics.12: Believers should eagerly look for the day of God, when the heavens and elements will be burned.
topics.13: A new heavens and earth are promised, where righteousness will dwell.
topics.14: Believers are urged to be diligent, living without spot or blemish in peace, ready for the Lord's return.
topics.15: The Lord's patience is salvation, as explained in Paul's letters, which are also addressed to believers.
topics.16: Paul's letters contain hard-to-understand truths that the ignorant twist to their own harm.
topics.17: Believers are warned to guard against false teachings and not fall from their strong foundation.
topics.18: Believers are encouraged to grow in grace and knowledge of Jesus Christ, with praise to him forever.

topics.1: Eyewitnesses describe what they saw and touched about Jesus, the Word of life.
topics.2: The eternal life of Jesus was with God and appeared to people.
topics.3: The writers share what they saw and heard so others can join their fellowship with God and Jesus.
topics.4: The writers write to make their joy complete through sharing with others.
topics.5: God is light, and there is no darkness in him.
topics.6: Claiming to be close to God but living in darkness is lying and not truthful.
topics.7: Walking in the light brings fellowship with God and cleansing from sin through Jesus' blood.
topics.8: Saying we have no sin is self-deception and truth is not in us.
topics.9: Confessing our sins leads to God forgiving and cleansing us.
topics.10: Saying we have not sinned makes God a liar and his message is not in us.

topics.1: Jesus helps people who sin, offering forgiveness and guidance.
topics.2: Jesus' sacrifice covers all sins, not just for believers but for everyone.
topics.3: Following Jesus' commands shows we truly know him.
topics.4: Claiming to know Jesus but not obeying him is a lie.
topics.5: Keeping Jesus' word completes God's love in us.
topics.6: Staying with Jesus means living as he lived.
topics.7: The command to love is not new but has been known since the beginning.
topics.8: A new command to love is given as the world moves toward truth.
topics.9: Hating others while claiming to be in the light is still in darkness.
topics.10: Loving others shows we are in the light and not causing others to stumble.
topics.11: Hating others keeps you in darkness, unaware of your direction.
topics.12: Your sins are forgiven because of Jesus' name.
topics.13: Older believers know Jesus from the beginning; younger ones have overcome evil.
topics.14: Children know God the Father; older believers know the eternal one; young ones are strong in God's word.
topics.15: Loving the world means the love of God is not in you.
topics.16: Worldly desires come from the world, not from God.
topics.17: The world and its desires are temporary; those who do God's will remain forever.
topics.18: The last hour has come, and many false teachers are already here.
topics.19: False teachers left the community because they were not truly part of it.
topics.20: You have the Holy Spirit's guidance and you all recognize it.
topics.21: You know the truth, and truth does not produce lies.
topics.22: Denying Jesus is the Christ is the mark of the Antichrist.
topics.23: Denying the Son means you also deny the Father; acknowledging the Son means you have the Father.
topics.24: Hold on to what you learned from the beginning to remain in God.
topics.25: God promised eternal life to those who believe.
topics.26: These teachings are about people trying to lead you astray.
topics.27: The Holy Spirit teaches you and you don't need others to teach you.
topics.28: Stay in Jesus so you will be confident and not ashamed when he returns.
topics.29: Doing what is right shows you are born from God.

topics.1: God's love for believers and calling them his children, which the world doesn't understand
topics.2: Believers are God's children now, and will be like Jesus when he appears
topics.3: Hope in Jesus leads to purity, as he is pure
topics.4: Sin is lawlessness, breaking God's standards
topics.5: Jesus came to remove sin, and he is without sin
topics.6: Those who stay in Jesus don't sin, but those who do haven't known him
topics.7: Don't be deceived, doing what is right makes you righteous like Jesus

topics.9: God's children don't sin because God's nature is in them

topics.11: The message from the beginning is to love each other
topics.12: Cain murdered his brother because his actions were evil
topics.13: The world will hate believers, don't be surprised
topics.14: Loving brothers shows we are alive in Christ, not in death
topics.15: Hating a brother is murder, and they won't have eternal life
topics.16: Jesus gave his life for us, so we should give our lives for others

topics.19: Doing what is right brings peace with God

topics.21: If our hearts are not accusing us, we can be bold with God
topics.22: God answers our prayers when we obey him and do what pleases him
topics.23: Believing in Jesus and loving others is God's command
topics.24: Staying in Jesus means he stays in us, shown by the Holy Spirit

topics.2: Recognizing the spirit of God by confessing Jesus came in the flesh
topics.3: Spirits that do not confess Jesus are from the Antichrist already in the world

topics.10: Love is shown by God loving us and sending his Son as a sacrifice for sins
topics.11: Since God loved us, we must love one another
topics.12: Loving one another means God lives in us and his love is complete
topics.13: We know God is in us because he gave us his Spirit
topics.14: Jesus was sent by the Father to save the world
topics.15: Confessing Jesus is the Son of God means God lives in us
topics.16: God is love and those who remain in love remain in God
topics.17: Perfect love gives confidence on the day of judgment
topics.18: Perfect love removes fear because fear is about punishment
topics.19: We love because God loved us first
topics.20: Claiming to love God but hating a brother is a lie
topics.21: Loving God means also loving your brother

topics.1: Believing Jesus is the Messiah means being born of God, and loving God means loving His children.
topics.2: Loving God's children means loving God and following His commands.
topics.3: God's commands are not a burden, and keeping them is how we show love for Him.
topics.4: Those born of God overcome the world through faith in Jesus.
topics.5: The only one who can overcome the world is the one who believes Jesus is God's Son.
topics.6: Jesus came through water and blood, and the Holy Spirit confirms the truth.
topics.7: Three witnesses testify about Jesus: the Spirit, the water, and the blood.
topics.8: The Spirit, the water, and the blood are one, all testifying about Jesus.
topics.9: God's testimony about His Son is greater than any human testimony.
topics.10: Believing in Jesus confirms God's testimony, but rejecting it makes someone a liar.
topics.11: God gave us eternal life, and that life is found in His Son Jesus.
topics.12: Having Jesus means having eternal life; without Him, there is no life.
topics.13: This letter is written so believers know they have eternal life through Jesus.

topics.15: If we know God hears us, we know our prayers are answered.
topics.16: Pray for a brother who sins but not to death, but don't pray for a sin that leads to death.
topics.17: All injustice is sin, but some sins don't lead to death.

topics.20: Jesus has come to give us truth and understanding, and He is the true God and eternal life.
topics.21: Children, protect yourselves from false gods and false worship.

topics.11: Greeting a false teacher means sharing in their evil deeds
topics.12: The writer wants to meet in person rather than write more, to bring full joy
topics.13: The children of the chosen sister send greetings

topics.2: The writer prays for Gaio's well-being and health, both physical and spiritual.
topics.3: The writer is happy that brothers have visited and confirmed Gaio's faithfulness.

topics.5: Gaio is praised for his faithful hospitality to fellow believers and strangers.
topics.6: The brothers have testified about Gaio's love in public, and he sends them off respectfully.
topics.7: The brothers traveled without taking anything from nonbelievers, for the sake of the name.

topics.13: The writer had more to say but prefers to speak in person rather than write it.
topics.14: The writer looks forward to meeting Gaio in person and speaking face to face.
topics.15: The letter ends with peace and greetings from friends, with a request to greet others by name.

topics.6: Jesus acknowledges the Ephesian church for hating the teachings of the Nicolaitans, which he also hates.
topics.7: Jesus promises the Ephesian church who conquer, the right to eat from the tree of life in God's paradise.

topics.9: Jesus acknowledges the Smyrna church's suffering and poverty, but calls them rich, and warns of Jewish false accusations.

topics.11: Jesus assures the Smyrna church that the one who conquers will not be harmed by the second death.

topics.9: People from all nations look at the bodies for three and a half days without burial.
topics.10: Those on earth rejoice over the witnesses and send gifts because they were tormented.
topics.11: After three and a half days, the witnesses are resurrected and cause fear.

topics.1: A beast rises from the sea with ten horns and seven heads, wearing crowns and carrying blasphemous names.

topics.4: People worship the dragon and the beast, asking who can defeat it.

topics.6: The beast blasphemes against God, His name, and those who live in heaven.

topics.8: Everyone on earth will worship the beast, except those whose names are in the Lamb’s book of life.
topics.9: A call to listen carefully to what is being said.
topics.10: Those taken into captivity will be captured, and those to be killed will be killed. This is the faith of the saints.
topics.11: Another beast rises from the earth, with horns like a lamb but speaks like a dragon.
topics.12: The second beast uses the authority of the first to force worship of the healed beast.
topics.13: The second beast performs great signs, even making fire come down from heaven.

topics.15: The image of the beast is given life and power to speak, and those who don’t worship it are killed.

topics.18: Wisdom is needed to understand the number of the beast, which is 666, the number of a human.
